dimensions.name: Record type selection
dimensions.rationale: Every plan item targets appropriate record types for the research question (identifying Thomas Flynn's death date to confirm parentage). Probate records would show Patrick as heir/son; church records would establish death date directly; tax records bracket the death year; land/deed records show estate settlement and father-son relationship; cemetery records confirm death date; newspaper death notices provide precise dates and survivors. Each rationale explains what specific information the record type provides (e.g., 'A will or letters of administration naming Patrick as a son or heir would be direct evidence of parentage'). Record types are well-justified for the 1860-1870 window.

dimensions.name: Sequencing logic
dimensions.rationale: Plan items follow defensible search order: probate (primary, indexed, FamilySearch) first; church records (indexed, FamilySearch) second; tax records (unindexed, courthouse/archives) third; land records (indexed, FamilySearch) fourth; cemetery (free, supporting) fifth; newspaper (mixed free/paid) sixth; Ancestry probate fallback (pli_007) seventh. The fallback chain is explicit: pli_008 (Ancestry probate) has fallback_for='pli_007', creating a clear dependency. Free/indexed sources precede paid/unindexed. Each rationale explains its placement (e.g., church records 'help anchor the probate search').

dimensions.name: Jurisdiction accuracy
dimensions.rationale: All jurisdictions are historically accurate for the 1860-1870 period. Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania existed and maintained probate, church, tax, land, and cemetery records throughout this window. The skill correctly identifies Schuylkill County Courthouse (Pottsville) and Pennsylvania State Archives (Harrisburg) as repositories for tax records. No anachronistic jurisdictions or pre-statehood errors. The plan correctly notes that Pennsylvania statewide civil death registration didn't begin until 1906, so death certificates are not planned for a ~1865 death.
